thread:
Tessa Morgan: Sharing the latest checklist UI variants for review. Goal: pick a direction for beta so Eng can start hardening the component. Figma link in thread 👇

Figma Bot: Tessa Morgan shared a file: “Guided onboarding checklist — UI variants” https://figma.com/file/redwood/console-checklist-variants?node-id=401%3A22

Kenji Nakamura: TL;DR we have 3 patterns in the file:
A) Persistent right sidebar (collapsible)
B) Modal “wizard” (step-by-step)
C) Dashboard card + deep links (lightweight)

Marissa Cole: thanks. question for design: are we trying to keep this always visible or only during first-run? I’m worried about shipping a thing that’s permanently taking up real estate.

Kenji Nakamura: yep that’s the core trade. Sidebar is great for “progress at a glance” + easy access, but it competes with the rest of Console nav/content.

Nikhil Sharma: I’m +1 to something that doesn’t interrupt. Modal makes me nervous — devs are here to copy/paste and run, modal blocking the page feels like we’re forcing a tour.

Tessa Morgan: agree. Modal wizard tested well in consumer onboarding, but for dev tools it can feel like “let me out” energy.

Hannah Rivera: from implementation POV: sidebar is easier than a modal that has to handle routing / keeping state when you close it / deep-link out to docs and back. Modal also tricky with back button behavior.

Dylan Brooks: also for E2E tests, persistent UI is way more stable. Modals tend to be flaky in Playwright (focus traps, overlays, timing).

George Mbatha: from research notes (last week): users said they wanted “a checklist somewhere I can come back to” vs “a tutorial.” That points to sidebar or dashboard card.

Wei Chen: docs angle: sidebar gives us consistent deep-link CTAs. If it’s a card only, we need to ensure users re-find it after they click out to docs.

Marissa Cole: can we talk about where it lives? In the variants, sidebar appears on most Console pages. Is that intended? I’d prefer it scoped to onboarding context (like project home + getting started).

Kenji Nakamura: variant A2 is “only on Project Overview + Usage” but there’s risk: if a step says “create API key,” user navigates to Keys page and checklist disappears.

Tessa Morgan: that’s why we explored persistent. But we can do a hybrid: checklist lives as a right-rail panel that’s available via a sticky “Onboarding” button, not always expanded.

Nikhil Sharma: +1 sticky entrypoint. Like Intercom launcher vibe but not chat.

Hannah Rivera: if it’s collapsed by default after first completion, can we store that preference server-side? Otherwise people will keep seeing it.

Dylan Brooks: we can store “dismissed/collapsed” locally (per browser) or server-side with the checklist state. ADR draft leans server-side for canonical state, but UI preference could be client.

Marissa Cole: preference should probably be client. Less privacy sensitivity, also avoids syncing UI quirks across users in org.

Kenji Nakamura: ok. Another big question: progress display. Sidebar variant uses: step list + status chips (Not started / In progress / Done) + checkmarks. Modal uses big CTA per step.

Tessa Morgan: I think we keep it scannable. For devs, the moment is “what’s next” not “read paragraphs.”

Wei Chen: copy note: we should keep step descriptions 1–2 lines max and push details to docs. Also consistent verbs (“Create”, “Make”, “Verify”, etc.). We have draft copy in DES-113 but it needs trimming.

Kenji Nakamura: accessibility: sidebar list needs proper focus order + keyboard nav for expand/collapse, and the progress indicators can’t be color-only.

Dylan Brooks: +1. Also remember smaller laptop widths. If sidebar forces content to 2/3 width it’ll be painful on dashboards.

Marissa Cole: re: dashboard card variant C — it’s lightweight, but I’m worried it won’t feel “guided” enough. We need step drop-off improvements.

George Mbatha: “guided” doesn’t mean modal. It can mean the checklist is context-aware. Ex: if step is “First request,” and we detect they already made one, it flips to done. That’s the guidance.

Nikhil Sharma: exactly. Also could highlight the next step as primary within the list (e.g., bold + “Recommended next”).

Kenji Nakamura: noted. In the designs, “Next up” is a pill at top + the next step highlighted. Could make that more obvious.

Tessa Morgan: let’s decide on direction:
- Modal wizard: strong guidance, but feels interruptive + routing/back button complexity
- Dashboard card: minimal intrusion, but discoverability and re-entry risk
- Sidebar/collapsible panel: persistent access + visible progress, but space cost

Marissa Cole: my vote: collapsible panel with a persistent entrypoint (button/tab). Default expanded for first-run, then collapses after user completes 2–3 steps or after dismissal.

Dylan Brooks: +1. Also helps us keep a single component shell for beta while we learn.

Hannah Rivera: if we do panel, can we align on behavior when navigating? Like panel stays open as you move pages within Console.

Kenji Nakamura: yes. Behavior spec proposal:
1) New orgs in cohort: panel auto-opens on first visit to Console after project creation
2) If user closes it, it stays closed for that browser until they manually open again
3) Panel icon/button persists across Console pages (top right)

Wei Chen: if panel is closed and user completes a step via validation (first request, streaming), do we show a subtle toast “Checklist updated” so they discover progress?

Tessa Morgan: great point. We should avoid noisy toasts though.

George Mbatha: maybe a small badge on the entrypoint button (“3/8”) that updates. That’s a passive nudge.

Kenji Nakamura: yes, badge w/ progress count.

Nikhil Sharma: can we ensure “deep links to docs” open in new tab? People will want to keep Console open.

Marissa Cole: agreed, but we also want attribution (UTM). There’s a separate ticket on UTM conventions.

Wei Chen: if opening new tab, we should include “opens in new tab” for a11y. Also consistent link style.

Dylan Brooks: for eng: I need design to call out what happens on mobile widths. Do we collapse into a bottom sheet? Or just a full-screen drawer?

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll add a responsive spec. Initial thought: at <1024px, panel becomes a slide-over drawer from right, full height, covering content. Entry button remains.

Tessa Morgan: also: step grouping. There’s a “First production launch” section that’s heavier. We should not dump 12 items in a single list.

Marissa Cole: agree. Grouping idea:
- Get started (key + first request)
- Build (streaming, structured output, error handling)
- Prepare for prod (prod key, rate limits, observability, safe rollout)
Then “First production launch” is basically that last group.

Kenji Nakamura: in variant A3 we had collapsible groups. I’ll iterate that.

Nikhil Sharma: ask: where do we put the “prod vs test key” step? It’s high friction right now. I want it early enough that people don’t hit SUP-9244 again.

Wei Chen: docs-wise it’s confusing early (“what is prod mode?”). Maybe keep it in Prepare for prod, but add a hint earlier: “Use a test key for experiments.”

George Mbatha: from interviews, people don’t know what environment they’re in until they get a 401. So earlier education might help even if they don’t create prod key yet.

Tessa Morgan: ok: we’ll keep prod key creation in Prepare for prod but add microcopy in “Create API key” step about test vs prod labeling.

Hannah Rivera: another implementation detail: if panel is persistent, and user clicks a step, does it navigate them to the right Console page? Or just open docs?

Kenji Nakamura: mix:
- For Console-native actions (create key, view usage): deep link into Console route
- For conceptual stuff (retries, streaming patterns): deep link to docs
Step row can have two CTAs? Might be too much.

Marissa Cole: keep single primary CTA per step. If it’s a Console action, route within Console. If it’s docs, open docs. Secondary link can be in overflow (“Learn more”).

Wei Chen: +1, single CTA. We can keep “Learn more” as inline text link in description.

Kenji Nakamura: cool. Action items I’m hearing:
1) Move forward with collapsible panel + persistent entrypoint button
2) Add grouping + collapsible sections
3) Add responsive behavior spec
4) Adjust copy to 1–2 lines + consistent verbs
5) Add passive progress badge on entrypoint (no spammy toasts)
6) Clarify navigation rules (Console route vs docs, single CTA)

Tessa Morgan: yep. Kenji can you push a v2 in Figma by EOW? Eng wants to start on shell next sprint.

Kenji Nakamura: will do. I’ll also annotate focus/keyboard interactions.

Dylan Brooks: thanks. Once v2 is ready, tag me and Hannah. We’ll sanity check feasibility + time.

Marissa Cole: and tag me + Nikhil for copy/step ordering. I want to lock that before beta cohort.

Wei Chen: please tag docs too. I’ll map each step to the canonical doc URL + confirm the “opens in new tab” language.

George Mbatha: I’ll add quick research notes summary to the ticket so we have rationale captured (modal aversion, preference for re-entry).

Tessa Morgan: perfect. :thumbsup: (also +1 to capturing rationale; we’ll need it when someone asks why we didn’t do a wizard)

Kenji Nakamura: ok closing loop — I’ll post v2 and we can do async feedback unless something urgent pops.
